reason: Both meet the structural requirements, but Response B enforces a stricter, less ambiguous snapshot-completion gate (it explicitly forbids proceeding on an 'in progress' or 'pending' snapshot) rather than allowing action once a snapshot is merely 'confirmed in-progress and crash-consistent,' which is a subtler judgment call that's riskier for an on-call responder to apply correctly. B also adds useful operational nuance (checking replica scope/lag in detection, branching to a secondary-cause investigation if latency persists after disk relief) that makes it marginally more actionable as a real runbook.
